followUp: A new build will use LAOZI_BUCK_RAW_SHIT.vst3 for both bundle and internal binary while preserving the Japanese display name. This isolates non-ASCII filesystem naming as a variable; it does not yet disprove the active Code Integrity policy.
trueCause: Windows Code Integrity rejected the Laozi VST3 executable before FL Studio could load it. The affected executable itself, not a child dependency, is named in the Code Integrity events.
affectedFilePath: C:\Program Files\Common Files\VST3\老子-BUCK RAW SHIT-.vst3\Contents\x86_64-win\老子-BUCK RAW SHIT-.vst3

dependencies.note: The loader was blocked by Code Integrity before dependency loading could be evaluated in FL Studio.

motw.reason: Neither the VST3 bundle root nor executable has a Zone.Identifier stream.

codeIntegrity.messageSummary: The exact VST3 executable did not meet Enterprise signing level requirements or violated Code Integrity policy.

unsignedComparison.conclusion: Their presence alone does not prove they successfully load under the active policy; no successful-load evidence was collected for them.

conclusions.codeSigningRequiredForThisPc: A signer allowed by the active Code Integrity policy is required. An arbitrary self-signed certificate may still be rejected.
conclusions.pcAppearsEnterpriseManaged: Active Code Integrity policy files, Enterprise signing-level rejection events, and enforced Code Integrity status strongly indicate managed or policy-enforced application control.

nextAction: Do not rebuild for this symptom. Ask the Windows/IT policy owner to allow the test signer or provide a signing certificate trusted by policy; alternatively validate the VST3 on a Windows machine without this enforcement.
